locator: II, lect. 2 n. 11: quod sit aliquod principium esse et veritatis rerum; et quod causae existentium non sunt infinitae, nec procedendo in directum secundum unam aliquam speciem causae
interpretation: Aquinas' paraphrase of Metaphysics II.2, 994a1-2, introduced because the preceding proof (n. 3-10: what causes being and truth in others is most true) would be removed if causes went on to infinity, there being then no first causes. Read as: for each perfection, the series of distinct causes of that perfection does not go on to infinity, formalized as well-foundedness (DEF-PERFECTION-CAUSE-REGRESS-ACCESSIBILITY). Reading step: the text indexes a line 'in directum' by one species of cause (material, efficient, final, formal, n. 12), and separately denies infinitely many species; this reading indexes the line by the perfection caused, as the lecture's own application to 'principium esse et veritatis' does. A line of causes of one perfection that alternates between species is not addressed by the sentence, and its inclusion belongs to the reading. The supporting arguments of Met II.2 (994a11-19 and following) are not derived.
